svg.aria-label: The four places a schema lives around one AWS Glue Data Catalog table, what each one does when the data changes, and the opposite column-access defaults of Parquet and ORC
svg.title: A table in the AWS Glue Data Catalog does not have one schema. A schema may be enforced upstream by the Glue Schema Registry, which rejects an incompatible version before it is ever written and offers eight compatibility modes with a hard cap of ten thousand schema versions per Region per account. The catalog then holds a table-level schema, which is what a crawler edits and what an UpdateBehavior of LOG freezes. It separately holds one schema per partition, which does not follow the table unless the crawler is configured with a Partitions AddOrUpdateBehavior of InheritFromTable. It also keeps a table version history, capped at one hundred thousand versions per table. Underneath all of that, the file format decides what a change means: Athena reads Parquet by name by default, so renaming a column breaks it while adding, removing and reordering are safe, and it reads ORC by index by default, which is the exact opposite. CSV and TSV allow new columns only at the end. And when schemas differ too much, a crawler's default is not to fail but to create two separate tables named after the partition values.

g.text: One table, four schemas — and each one drifts differently
None of these disagreeing raises an error. Two of them change what a query returns.
1. Glue Schema Registry
upstream of the producer
optional, and free to use
The only one that stops a change. Eight compatibility modes; BACKWARD is
the recommended one. DISABLED forbids new versions entirely.
Hard cap: 10,000 schema versions per Region per account. Not adjustable.
2. Table schema
Data Catalog, table level
what everyone means by it
What a crawler rewrites on every run. SchemaChangePolicy UpdateBehavior
of LOG freezes it. Tables AddOrUpdateBehavior of MergeNewColumns lets
new columns in but protects the ones you corrected by hand.
3. Partition schema
one per partition, and there
may be millions of them
Does not follow the table. Changing the table schema leaves every
existing partition on the old one.
Fix: Partitions AddOrUpdateBehavior = InheritFromTable.
4. Table version history
every edit keeps the old one
this is the audit trail
100,000 versions per table, and adjustable. An hourly crawler that
rewrote the schema on every single run would take about 11.4 years to
reach it. This is the one quota here that will not be your problem.
Underneath all four, the file format decides what a change means
Athena is schema-on-read. These are its defaults, and two of them are opposites.
PARQUET — read by name
parquet.column.index.access = false
Add anywhere, remove, reorder: safe
Rename a column: breaks
Set that property true to invert this.
ORC — read by index
orc.column.index.access = true
Rename a column: safe
Add in the middle, remove, reorder: no
The opposite default to Parquet.
CSV and TSV
no column names in the format
Rename, add at the end: safe
Remove, reorder, add at front: no
Position is the only identity here.
When two files under one prefix are not similar enough, the crawler does not fail.
It creates two tables named after the partition values — year_2017 and year_2018 — and reports success.
Grouping TableGroupingPolicy = CombineCompatibleSchemas asks for one table instead.
